questions.q: In the workshop requirement, why does the model end up needing only one new custom object (Workshop) instead of three?
options: Workshop, Instructor, and Attendee are not valid object names
Instructor and Attendee are both people, already covered by the standard Contact object
Salesforce limits orgs to one custom object
Custom objects cannot be related to each other
questions.explain: Following Lesson 20's reuse principle, Instructor and Attendee are both just people and are already covered by the standard Contact object, leaving only Workshop with no standard-object match.

questions.q: Why is Workshop's relationship to its Instructor modeled as a Lookup rather than a Master-Detail?
options: Master-Detail cannot connect to the Contact object
Lookup fields render faster than Master-Detail fields
Lookup is required whenever the parent is a standard object
It's a loose, one-to-many connection — deleting an Instructor's Contact record shouldn't force-delete every Workshop they taught
questions.explain: A Lookup is deliberately loose, which fits the business reality here: an instructor's departure shouldn't cascade-delete the workshops they once taught.

questions.q: Why does the Attendee side of the requirement need a junction object instead of a single relationship field?
options: Because junction objects are required for every relationship in Salesforce
Because Workshop is a custom object
Because it's a many-to-many relationship — an Attendee can register for many Workshops, and a Workshop has many Attendees
Because Contact cannot have any relationship fields
questions.explain: A single Master-Detail or Lookup field can only point to one parent, so modeling 'many on both sides' requires a junction object, as established in Lesson 17.

questions.q: Why does Workshop Registration use two Master-Detail relationships instead of two Lookups?
options: It was chosen arbitrarily with no real justification
Lookup relationships cannot be created on junction objects
Master-Detail is always faster to query than Lookup
A registration record has no meaning without both its Workshop and its Attendee, so the tight, cascading bond fits the actual business logic
questions.explain: The guide stresses that Master-Detail here reflects real business logic — a registration is meaningless without both parents — not just that Master-Detail happened to be available.

questions.q: If the requirement changed so that each Attendee could only ever attend exactly one Workshop, what would that change about the model?
options: Contact could no longer be used to represent Attendees
Workshop would need to become a standard object
Nothing — the junction object would still be required
The relationship would no longer be many-to-many, so a junction object would no longer be necessary; a direct Lookup or Master-Detail could replace it
questions.explain: Without 'many workshops per attendee,' the relationship collapses to one-to-many, which a single relationship field can model directly — no junction object needed.
